questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Polar Equation of a Circle Given a Point on the Circumference
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039331/assets/2abff4f1dcb5bfd305a5560293892828f94d3fe8cca755bec1998d4f3fda077f.png)

The polar equation of the circle centered at the origin that passes through the point $A(5,12)$, as shown above, is$\,\,r=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
A circle of radius $k$ centered at the origin has the polar equation $r=k.$

We can compute the radius $k$ of our circle using the Pythagorean theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169} \\  & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the circle is $r=13.$
